nodes.title: Compose resolves the SHELL over .env while the checker resolves .env over the shell — a green credential check over a stack running the shared literal
nodes.description:
## BLUF

`docker compose` resolves the **shell environment over the project** `.env`; `source` resolves the `.env` **over the shell**. The credential checker uses `source`. So in one shell, with one correctly-rotated `.env`, **the checker prints a full green bill of health and** `rc=0` **while compose resolves both datastore passwords to the shared literals from git history.**

This is **F-800-05 reopened by a new route** — a confident green over an exposed stack — and it lands on the surface Stuart and Peter are asked to trust on rotation day (`APP_DB_PASSWORD` rotation 2026-09-05 09:00).

Found by the compose-precedence probe named as the highest-value next step in the 2026-09-04 through-code gate on #800's fix round. **No fix is written.** Filed separately from #800 on Wednesday's ruling: the fix is a behaviour change to the start path, not a change to the checker's parser.

## Recommendation

Fix on its own branch off `develop`, not on #800. Two candidate shapes, neither chosen here:

* **(a)** have `start-environment.sh` source `.env` on the same path, so the shell and compose agree — this also makes FR-1's safety claim true, which is the same defect from the other side; or
* **(b)** have the checker "be the consumer" for real: read the values the way compose does (shell first, `.env` second) rather than the way `source` does.

**(b) is the one that matches what the script claims about itself.** See the claim-defect below.

## Detail

### The measurement, and why the discriminator is the keeper

`${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-secuura_dev_password}` means **the compose default IS the shared literal**. So a naive probe — export the shared literal, see whether compose renders the shared literal — **cannot distinguish "the shell won" from "compose saw nothing and fell back to its default."** It returns the alarming-looking answer for the reassuring reason, or the reassuring answer for no reason at all.

A **three-way sentinel** was used instead:

| rendered value | meaning |
| -- | -- |
| `rotated_probe_pg_A1` (the fixture) | the `.env` won — no inversion |
| `AMBIENT_SHELL_pg_B2` (the sentinel) | **the shell won — inversion real** |
| `secuura_dev_password` (compose default) | neither was seen — the probe did not vary its subject |

Result, `docker compose config` only (render-only; no `-o`, no `--lock-image-digests`, no `up`), fixture supplied via `--env-file` from a scratchpad file:

| run | interp-env PG | interp-env Redis | rendered postgres service |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **CONTROL** — no ambient export | fixture wins | fixture wins | fixture wins |
| **TREATMENT** — shell exports sentinel | **SHELL WINS** | **SHELL WINS** | **SHELL WINS** |

**The control is what makes the treatment readable.** It proves `--env-file` was honoured, that the fixture is genuinely the file compose read, and — since nothing unrecognised appeared — that no real `.env` leaked into the probe. The only thing differing between the two runs is the ambient export.

### The real-world shape, both instruments in one shell

Shell still exports the old shared literals; `.env` correctly rotated:

* **checker** → `✓ POSTGRES_PASSWORD is per-clone`, `✓ REDIS_PASSWORD is per-clone`, `rc=0`
* **compose** → `POSTGRES_PASSWORD=secuura_dev_password`, `REDIS_PASSWORD=secuura_redis_dev`

### The claim in shipped source that this refutes

`check-slot-credentials.sh:96-99` carries the justification for the entire sourcing design:

> *"it cannot drift from the consumer, **because it IS the consumer**."*

It is not the consumer. Compose is, and compose resolves with the opposite precedence. (The sentence itself is being corrected on #800's branch alongside FR-1/FR-6; the behavioural fix is this ticket.)

### Blast radius — bounded, and it lands on FR-1's caller

Measured per caller at `e26cfce2b`, with a bash-semantics control:

* `start-local.sh` — checker L63, `source .env` L103 with **no** `set -a`. A plain assignment to an **already-exported** variable keeps the export attribute and updates the value, so the stale ambient **is overwritten** by the rotated `.env` before compose runs. Control: with the variable not previously exported, a child process sees nothing. **This path is neutralised — by accident. Nothing anywhere records that the L103** `source` **is load-bearing**, so moving or removing it silently opens this hole.
* `start-environment.sh` — checker L91, **no** `source` **anywhere in its 283 lines**, `docker compose up` L135. The stale export survives untouched from the operator's shell into compose. **This is the live path, and it is the same caller QA FR-1 named.**

### The precondition is self-priming

`check-slot-credentials.sh:164`, in the UNREADABLE arm, tells the operator:

> `See the parse error with:  sh -n '<file>'  (or: set -a; . '<file>')`

**Running that second form in an interactive shell is exactly the act that exports these two variables into it.** So the script hands the operator the command that arms the trap — and the operator most likely to type it is the one whose `.env` is malformed, i.e. mid-rotation. (The suggestion is being dropped from that message on #800's branch as part of the upgraded FR-8; that removes one route to the precondition, **not** the precedence defect itself.)

### Not established

Whether `start-environment.sh` runs anywhere but a developer laptop — laptop only, or also the demo/UAT VM. That bounds the severity and it was not settled from the tree.

---

Discovered 2026-09-04 (s122) by the compose-precedence probe. Related: PR #800 (`e26cfce2b`), QA FR-1 (same caller), QA FR-8 (the self-priming message).
